this app is SO GOOD. im new to the workout field, and wanted something that didn’t yell in my face every day that i was not working out the recommended 30 minutes a day, that i wasn’t reaching my goals on certain days, etc. i am someone that needs a slow and steady pace, and thats exactly what this app has given me. now after using it with premium for a month, i am excited to open my app every day and see where my activity level should be and get my walk in everyday, as well as review my metrics to see how far i’ve come from last month. i appreciate the new update and cant wait to see how next month goes! HIGHLY recommend this app.

title.label: It’s not just about PACE…it’s about peace of mind!

content.label:
The "Gentler Streak" fitness app encourages a self-compassionate approach to exercise and provides a balance between fitness and rest. It offers personalized suggestions for daily workout actions, which can range from rest to intense workouts. It helps me - a 67 year old guy who values a balanced approach to fitness and well-being - stay within healthy activity levels. 

With an intuitive UI, it’s so easy to use, even my grandma could do it—and she can’t tell a smartwatch from her headstone. It’s easy to understand and won’t leave you sweating the small stuff.

The app’s feedback is so encouraging, it’s like having a cheerleader in your pocket. It’ll lift your spirits higher than a kettlebell! 
Additionally, the app provides relevant, actionable insights and expert knowledge in short reads. 

It earns 5 👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼 from me!

title.label: No trial period for most features.

content.label: I was really excited to use this app, since I frankly find the Apple Health app unusable in terms of understanding metrics, but I was super disappointed because basically all of the features are locked behind the paywall. To be clear, I’m not against paying for an app that works and is genuinely helpful, but if I can’t see what I’m paying for, then why should I spend any money? They advertise a 48-hour promotion to buy an annual subscription… why not give us a 48-hour trial to even see if it’s worth it?
This app has alot of potential but the problem is its very expensive i wish the prices were affordable or reasonable at very least!

I love gentler streak. I find it very motivational and as someone with some chronic health issues I like that it has an option for when you are sick. It also has been able to accurately predict me getting sick with a cold like 3 times now. Which is sort of cool.
I love this app. If it had the ability to track habits, especially if trying to quit something like vaping, it would actually be the best tool for overall health and wellness.
I like the way this app approaches activities and well being with compassion. It’s just the right amount of nudging without nagging or making me feel like I’m competing against myself.

There was a time in my life when I was an Ironman triathlete, but a combination of COVID, heavy workload and aging had my fitness levels drop significantly over recent years. Gentler Streaks has been fantastic in helping me to get back into shape, giving me a supportive and *gentle* push to gradually increase my activity without wearing myself out or yo-yo’ing into and out of cycles of exercise. The interface is great and easy to follow, the technical side of the app is excellent, and the feedback is fun. I use this app everyday and find it to be a great compliment to Apple Fitness+.

title.label: Pretty App to Designed to Keep You On the Sofa

content.label:
It’s a cute app, and I love the concept. 

However, I am accustomed to 2-3 workouts a week. These vary intensity. My Apple Watch says my cardio fitness is “above average” and I feel I have normal recovery times. I’m far from a fitness junky, but like average fit I’d say. 

I just came back to logging after taking a break (but not a break from working out) and gentler streak tells me my 27 minute gentle Pilates session (my heart rate was in zones “0” and “1” according to Gentler puts me into “over exertion”. That going for a slow walk for the morning after is “too much”. 

If you want an app that congratulates you for doing a singular workout and gives you an excuse to “rest” for days after any moderate effort … Sign on up. If you actually want something to give you insights on your health and fitness and encourages you to improve, move along.
Useful and addictive.

This app is such a great tool when paired with the Apple Watch. I love that it gives me grace when I really don’t want to workout and pushes me when I need to get back on track. It’s like having a personal fitness coach!

title.label: BEST workout tracker !!! With one request

content.label:
I ADORE this app!! I have a pretty bad tendency to push myself too hard when I workout, and this app has helped me so much to always have an idea of where my body is at and if I need to back off. It helps me stay on track and lets me know when I need to get a workout in (wouldn’t want to lose my streak of course). I especially love that the messages are written like a friend encouraging you to stay with it and keep going without being harsh or feeling shameful. 

The one feature that would make this so much better is if there was a notes section inside each activity after they’ve been completed. When you open the activities tab and select a recently completed activity, I imagine that there could be a “notes” section under “charts” and “perceived exertion.” I usually record my workouts as “strength training” but have a tendency to forget when the last time was that I worked a certain muscle group. As a college student I can’t always go to the gym consistently so I get workouts in when I can. This means I don’t have a set weekly workout schedule and must try to remember the last time I hit legs lol. Having a section for notes would make it so much easier to remember when I did certain workouts, or it could even be used as a way to track weight and reps for the day. I’ve been trying to find a way to track these things either on my own or in an app and it just doesn’t seem like anything exists for this purpose and/or is easy to use. In addition to a notes section, it could be helpful to be able to add a title or subtitle to an activity to more easily identify details about it. This could look like “strength training - Legs” where the original title of the activity remains, but you are able to add quick details to the log. 
I already love this app so much and use it for every workout, but if this feature could be added my love for gentler would just grow even more. I think it would really enhance the already amazing experience and make workout tracking that much easier.

If you need to use the app for a few weeks until stops telling you that you need to rest because it doesn’t know you is totally discouraging and useless. The app is cute but I can’t keep associating my heart with one that is in pain when im perfectly fine, i walk and i do weights period. You guys need to tweek this for starting users that have highly active lifestyles. The app wants you to stop doing what you doing and live in resting move because it doesn’t know your resting heart rate average, but if you want to lower your resting heart rate you need to move friends, don’t listen to this app!

title.label: Great for Novice, not great for serious training

content.label:
I love that Gentler Streak makes it simple and easy for folks who are just beginning their fitness journey. However, if you are a serious athlete training for a marathon, 15 K, or some other endurance race this is probably not the app for you. I have been training for eight weeks and recently completed a 8 mile run. I took a day off to recover, and then the following day the app said I was pushing too hard, 1 mile in to a 2 mile active recovery run. I know my body and I know when it is time to lay off. Being in tune with my body and whether or not, it’s ready after recovery is something that comes with years of training and experience.

Again, this is great for those just beginning, or just wanting to learn about their body and it’s response to stress from physical activity. It is not meant for rigorous and experienced endurance athletes.

title.label: Needs at least a minor trial of premium features

content.label: I have no problem paying for quality apps, but to demand a year sub without even a small free trial of the premium features is silly. The free functions are useless as Apple health gives you the same data. The UX is visually appealing though and I could see myself subscribing if I was able to at least check out what I was subscribing to.

title.label: Go Gentler isn’t perfect, but it’s at the head of its class!

content.label: To get a stats summary and AI encouragement that nicely replaces a live coach, all at a reasonable price, is wonderful. This program can work for almost anyone if it can work for me as nicely as it does! DDD -(desperate deteriorating dinasour).

I love this app! I’ve used it for a while now, and I found it is the best way to maintain a healthy lifestyle. I would recommend this app to anyone who wants to get healthier, or just wants help keeping their fitness habits alive.

title.label: Gentler Streak is an excellent App to pair with your Apple Watch!

content.label: I have had Gentler Streak for about a year now and it’s an awesome App to sync with your Apple Watch. It gives more insights into your health. The only issue I’ve noticed was that the Apple Health App will show an increase in all activity like exercise and move activity due to the information being shared to Health. It’s almost like it’s tracking workouts as double. Other than that, it’s just great and convenient to have.

This. Is the first activity/fitness app that I’ve found worth the price.  It can capture any activity you might do!  I’m still working out some challenges with capturing all the data I want to track, it shows as an option, but it’s not tracking with each activity. I’ll figure that out though.  In the meantime, I’m so happy with this I’ve gone with the lifetime subscription!

But I’m not a fan of paying for the annual subscription and not have access to the full features because I’m not wearing a smart watch during sleep.

I guess I can come back if I ever find something that tracks my sleep that I like, but until then, I won’t be renewing.

Great app - can tell when I’m about to get sick or just when I should have a rest day. If I’m not sure what type of exercise to do, it gives recommendations and sometimes it says to just rest. I can’t trust my own judgement or know when I’m sick, so I let this app drive and I’ve been happy with it.

title.label: Stop comparing activity to food consumed

content.label:
I enjoy this app, but I can’t recommend it to a friend who would love it because you compare calories burned to food. She has an eating disorder, and if you won’t take this feature off the app altogether, it should at least be something you can turn off.

Its harmful to think about movement this way. If this app is meant to be gentler, then we need to motivate movement for our wellbeing, not to counteract what we put in our bodies to stay alive.

In my opinion, this app doesn’t really measure activity well; it frequently tells me I’m over reaching to the point where I don’t even log workouts—a thirty minute walk plus 30 minutes of yoga is not over reaching, at least not for me. I get that for some people it might be, but with my current fitness levels and history of amount of time working out, the app should know after three months that this is a normal amount of activity for me. I guess if you want to be very, very gently coaxed into doing a bit more activity, this app will work, but if you want to challenge yourself and if you’re already fairly active, I’d suggest looking elsewhere.

title.label: This is the BEST health, wellness, and fitness tracker I’ve ever used

content.label:
I became aware of this app at the beginning of 2023 after searching for one to help me with my New Year resolution. I wanted to assess better when to work out and which type I’ll do for each day. 

Each morning, this app helps me improve my self-care because of the metrics it provides about my previous night. I tried the one-week free trial before purchasing my annual subscription. Over the last year, I followed the Gentler Streak recommendation, and it has helped improve my wellness overall. 

I realized I was pushing too hard during some workouts and was not well enough to exercise on other days. Recommended rest days were always impactful. 

I encourage anyone who wishes to improve their self-care more compassionately to start the same journey I did with this app. You won't regret it.

This app sounded so promising that I paid the $55 to have the premium subscription only to find out that the team is unresponsive to emails and my premium access was never applied and I was never able to use the app as promised.

I have garmin watch so I don’t have Apple which is fine with me, but so much hidden features behind the pay wall. It is very pricey! So much things missing as well the steps part and the calories burned a day besides workouts alone. 👏 my question is doesn’t it work for Apple AirPod pro 2?! The overall I love the app!

This is the dumbest exercise app I have ever had. There are no workouts in the app that can gradually increase your activity. If there are workouts I can’t find them. You get to choose rest days. Sounds good right? You can chooses one every day if you want

Gentler works well as an accessory to the health app. Synced metrics are made easy to understand and personalized goals encourage a balanced lifestyle. Though it does seem extra cautious about over-exertion (but maybe that’s just me). Most importantly, it’s very cute!
For some reason after the update last week, the complication icon will not appear on the watch. I’ve deleted and reloaded several times and still no luck.
The fitness app is like having a personal trainer in my pocket. The workouts are fun, and it tracks my progress, making me feel accomplished. Definitely worth the download! 5/5 stars.

I’ve had this app for a few months and I LOVE it. It gives me motivation and tells me when to relax for a day or two. I decided to go premium and honestly it just didn’t do anything for me. The little articles it gives you and recommended workouts are not anything special. Don’t go premium, but definitely use the free version.

title.label: Fantastic App - cute and well thought out

content.label: I do really like this App - it gives me thoughtful and valuable insights into my Health status and into my Fitness behavior. The watch app with the zones are my most favorite part. And thankfully there is a reasonable option to purchase a discounted Lifetime version (I hate apps with only subscription models…).
Issues syncing between iPhone app and Apple Watch continue and the devs do nothing about it for a year now. 👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻 Reaching the end of my patience with this app. Otherwise had some potential.

I’ve had the app for a few days now and all it tells me is I’m overreacting. It never changes. I got for 5 mile walks daily and have for the past year. I also hit the stationary bike for half hour daily and it doesn’t change. App is kinda garbage. I’d find a different app.

title.label: The best workout app I’ve ever used

content.label: I never write app reviews, but as a college student with little time for herself this app changed my life. It helps me put not only my fitness first, but rest. I love the sustainable approach to health, and find myself the most in shape I’ve been since high school. It helps me push myself and know when to take a break. I would recommend it to absolutely everyone I know. The subscription is so worth it too, get this app!!!!
Apple would not give a refund. I accidentally subscribed. I have deleted this. Keep my money

I just started using the app 2 weeks ago. So far I find the app informative and easy to use. Looking forward to digging into it and using info it gives me. I had questions while setting up premium app and used the contact us part. I emailed them at 5am EST this morning and got a response within 5 minutes. They walked me through it so I can understand it and made sure all my questions were answered. First time impression was excellent. Looking forward to getting all I can from this app.

title.label: Just not enough to warrant a subscription

content.label:
It’s cute and all but $20 / yr to look at a line graph is not worth it. 

Also not happy that when they tried to incentivise me to come back on board they hid all my workout data!
Instantly deleted app and now even happier with my decision.

I basically never write reviews but this app deserves it. I have used this app for just under one year. I struggled a lot with finding time for exercise both because of busy schedules and mental health. This app allowed me to feel good about even little accomplishments and helped me get the momentum to keep trying. There’s a break/sick/vacation option that’s the major bonus over apple health/rings because you don’t feel awful if you need to take time to heal. Highly recommended!!

title.label: A perfect alternative to Apple Fitness

content.label:
I love the personalized approach to fitness on this app! I still use my Apple Watch activity app to track my workouts since it’s what I’m familiar with, but I love that the two apps talk to each other back and forth so I can go into gentler streak and see my heart rate zones and understand when I might be overdoing it. 

A way way way more personal and maintainable approach to fitness, that doesn’t require you to set any unrealistic goals that you won’t stick with, and doesn’t focus on weight loss/calories.

title.label: After searching for over a decade…

content.label: This is the only workout app that has made me want to work out. The fact that it counts rest days as productive and encourages you not to lose your streak in a gentle way, is the best! Other apps are just about checking something off or marking it done, and when you miss one, you feel terrible. This gives you flexibility and as long as you’re in the progress zone, you’re good! Also love it talks to the health app, so if I’m doing a workout with another app that talks to the health app, Gentle Streak marks it too. Love love love this app!

title.label: Don’t use if you’re interested in increasing fitness

content.label: This app is not for anyone looking to improve their fitness level. Any time I actually exercise, it cries at me or chastises me and calls me an overachiever. And I mean, if all I do is a slow 3 mile jog or a moderate 30 minute strength training session, it gives me grief. The only days I don’t get chewed out by this app are days that I am not exercising. I tried it for two months to see if I could figure out how to increase my fitness activity without it whining at me or complaining, and I never could. Deleting. Waste of money.
